title: color_rgba element check tests stale `ok` (the json.Object assert), not `okc` — non-integer elements silently become 0 instead of failing fast
detail: `!ok` refers to the outer `obj, ok := v.(json.Object)`, always true here, so the type-mismatch branch is dead: a float/string element (parse_integers keeps floats as json.Float) fails the `.(json.Integer)` assert (okc=false, n=0) yet passes validation as 0. Malformed JSON silently accepted — defeats the new loader's ODN-5 fail-fast intent. `okc` is declared and never used.
recommended_fix: Change the guard to `if !okc || n < 0 || n > 255` so a non-integer color_rgba element returns the named error instead of defaulting to 0.

title: default_lane truncated to u8 BEFORE the >2 range check (both packet_types and demand entries) — values congruent to 0/1/2 mod 256 silently pass wrapped
detail: jint returns i32; u8() wraps before validation: 256→0 (Express), 257→1, -256→0 all pass the >2 check silently with a different lane than authored. Only values wrapping to 3..255 are rejected. ODN-5 fail-fast gap in the new 3.1 loaders.
recommended_fix: Range-check the i32 from jint before narrowing (e.g. `dl := jint(...); if dl < 0 || dl > 2 { return ... }; pt.default_lane = u8(dl)`) at both sites.

title: set-piece start_tick/duration_ticks/forecast_lead_ticks wrap negative i32 to huge u64 with no negativity check — a malformed set-piece silently never fires
detail: jint can return negative i32; u64(-5) wraps to ~2^64-5. duration_ticks==-5 passes (only ==0 checked); a negative start_tick makes set_piece_active's `tick >= sp.start_tick` false forever — the surge silently never activates. ODN-5 fail-fast gap in the new set-piece loader.
recommended_fix: Validate each tick field's i32 >= 0 before the u64 conversion (duration_ticks > 0), returning the named catalog error on negatives.

title: duplicate `era` rows in demand.json silently overwrite — the earlier row's entries/set_pieces are dropped and their arrays leak
detail: No duplicate-era check: a second row with the same `era` overwrites eras[era-1]; the first row's demand content is silently lost and its entries/set_pieces dynamic arrays are never stored nor freed (catalogs_destroy only frees the stored rows). ODN-5 fail-fast gap in the new demand loader.
recommended_fix: Track populated eras (or check entries/set_pieces non-nil at era-1) and return a named error on a duplicate era row before overwriting.
